entire repo mirror add — Mirror a repository onto one or more clusters
With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs. --cluster requires a <repo>.

With a <repo>, places it on every cluster named by --cluster — repeat the flag or comma-separate the hosts — in parallel, then waits for each to become usable. Pass --no-wait to return as soon as the placements are registered. Idempotent on (repo, cluster), so naming a cluster the repo is already on reports it rather than failing.

When --cluster is omitted, an interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a multi-select; non-interactive runs default to aws-us-east-2.entire.io.

With an /et/ ref, places replicas of an Entire-native repo and waits for each to be seeded. A native mirror goes in a region other than the repo's own, so only those clusters are offered and --cluster has no default there: non-interactive runs must name one.

Every cluster is attempted: one that fails does not stop the others, and the command exits non-zero naming the ones that did.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Examples:
entire repo mirror add
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /et/acme/web --cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io

entire repo remote add — Point a git remote in this clone at an Entire cluster
Adds a git remote so fetch and push go through Entire instead of the forge.

An Orca plugin that brings Entire trails, findings and checkpoints into Orca. The plan, the API limits
it works within, and the spike results are in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).

Requires Orca 1.4.245 or later, and the Entire CLI logged in wherever your repos live (WSL or Windows).

## Setting up the code review trail

Entire's code review is `entire review`. Several reviewer agents review the branch in parallel, then a judge merges their reports. With the output set to `trail`, the verdict is posted on the branch's trail as findings, so it shows in Orca's Entire panel. This repo has no review profile yet. Setting one up is your command to run, so here is one you can paste into PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT='1'
entire review --configure `
  --set-slot claude-code=opus --set-slot codex `
  --set-judge claude-code=opus `
  --set-output trail `
  --set-task "Review this branch of an Orca trusted-worker plugin. Check correctness, Windows/WSL/SSH path handling, the 30-second command budget, and that text read from Entire or Orca is only rendered, never executed or passed to a shell. Follow CLAUDE.md."
```

- **Reviewers:** Claude Opus and Codex review independently, and Opus judges. These are the review agents your CLI offers; Pi is the other one.
- **Shared profile:** without `--local`, the profile goes into `.entire/settings.json`, which is committed, so commit it and every clone gets it. Add `--local` to keep it to yourself.
- **Wizard:** to choose these settings interactively, run `entire review --configure` with no other flags.

## Running a review

The review needs a branch that is linked to a trail. For the SSH work:

```powershell
git switch -c vps-ssh          # takes your uncommitted changes along
# commit, then:
git push -u origin vps-ssh
entire trail link 378 --branch vps-ssh
entire review                  # findings land on trail #378
```

You can also review from anywhere with `entire review --target https://entire.com/gh/petercr/-/trails/378`. It checks the branch out in a separate worktree first.

I fixed the Code review finding and pushed it to the PR branch (commit `5733329`). The push should start a new cloud review on https://entire.com/gh/petercr/-/trails/378.

**The bug:** `serverSshTarget` saved each server's SSH target in a module-level map for the life of the worker. The worker now runs until Orca quits. So if you edited the target or re-paired the server, refreshes kept connecting to the old address until the plugin was turned off and on.

**The fix:** in `src/worker/ssh-targets.mjs` I removed the cache, so the target is looked up again on every refresh. A server refresh already makes several `orca` CLI calls, and this adds one more plus a read-only SQLite query. It runs only when a refresh happens, not on the 5-second focus poll. I added a code comment explaining why it isn't cached.

**Test:** the two lookups can now be swapped for fakes in tests. A new test changes the saved address, switches the server to a different target, and then removes the target. It checks that each lookup picks up the change, which the old cache would have failed. All 64 tests pass.
